oliver: Quick thread: customer connectivity options for private control-plane auth when peering/VPCE is not acceptable. I sketched 3 patterns and tradeoffs.
mina: please share patterns.
oliver: 1) operatorless ephemeral tunnels -> no customer infra changes, on-demand TLS tunnels to regional relays. Pros: low friction. Cons: dynamic egress IPs, relay scaling, slightly higher tail latency.
raj: 2) pinned-connector binary -> small connector that pins to a customer-provided ENI or static NAT gateway. Pros: stable egress IP for allowlists, predictable perf. Cons: requires customer ops + lifecycle.
mina: 3) managed mini-gateway (our IaC deployed into customer account) -> gives static egress but we operate minimal infra in their account. Pros: less customer toil than full peering. Cons: requires cross-account role and support process.
infra-bot: note: ensure any managed infra uses least-privilege roles and explicit expiry for CloudFormation stacks.
oliver: auth flow idea: scoped onboarding token -> /auth/exchange -> short-lived mTLS certs (TTL 5m). Short TTL reduces CRL needs.
carmen: ops: measure connection churn. Recommend default keepalive 60s and a warm-window option for enterprise. Also add p95 handshake metric.
raj: perf note: relay hop adds ~10-25ms depending on region. Document guidance: peering for sub-50ms, managed-gateway for allowlist, ephemeral by default.
mina: security: tokens must be region-scoped and logged. Add an opt-in checkbox during token issuance: "allow agentless connectivity".
oliver: rollout: preview with 10 non-prod customers + telemetry (handshake_ms p50/p95, conn/sec, nat_bytes). Gate: p95 handshake <300ms and relay CPU <70%.
infra-bot: action: ARCH-conn-preview created (link: https://go/arch/ARCH-conn-preview).
mina: thanks. I'll help draft the RFC with diagrams and test matrix.
oliver: will post RFC link here when ready.
